# Audio loudness report (R22, generated by `node tools/dev/loudness-report.mjs --write`)

Read from `validation/audio.json` (203 sounds, 2 music renders, measured 2026-10-20T01:04:38.345Z at commit df3c274). **Every number here is a sound rendered ALONE, offline.** Nothing in this file says how loud the game is when a gun, a creature and the score play together through the master chain; that is a LISTENING question and belongs to the owner. This report only finds the sounds most likely to stand out, so the listening pass can start with them. No gain was changed because of it.

Levels are dB full scale: the loudest 100 ms window of the sound (its "punch"; what an ear weighs a short sound by) and its sample peak. A 6 dB difference is about twice as loud. A family is a group a player hears as one kind of thing (`FAMILIES` in the tool).

The median sound's loudest window is −19.8 dBFS; the sounds span −38.3 to −7.3 dBFS (31.1 dB).

## The score against the effects

- calm music: loudest window −29.0 dBFS, −9.2 dB against the median effect (peak −20.3).
- combat music: loudest window −17.1 dBFS, 2.7 dB against the median effect (peak −7.9).

The game mixes the score under the effects by its own bus gains; the offline render of the score alone cannot say whether it is too quiet or too loud in play. Listen to a fight on a map with the score running.

## How to use this

1. Play two or three maps with headphones and with the speakers you expect players to have, once with music and once with the effect volume alone. Note, per sound, "too loud", "too quiet" or "fine" against this list (the Record of the owner's listening pass can be a plain list of ids).
2. A gain change is a change to a recipe in `src/audio/synth.js` (or its bus level in `src/audio/engine.js`) and a new `npm run audio-qa`. The audio code is one of the source sets every map's evidence depends on, so the change goes before the single evidence regeneration (R26).
3. `tests/loudness.test.js` holds the bounds that must always be true (no clipping, nothing inaudible, every sound in a family); it does not hold the balance, which only ears can.
